## CHOLANGITIS
Oral step-down treatment
Most cases are due to common bile duct obstruction. Obstruction (if present)
must be relieved with an endoscopical, transcutaneous, or surgical procedure.
The most common pathogens isolated are E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterococcus and
Enterobacter. Pseudomonas coverage is recommended in severe (grade 3)
cholangitis. Anaerobic coverage is recommended if biliary-enteric abnormality
is present.
Antimicrobials' role in cholangitis is to allow patients to have elective and
not emergently scheduled drainage procedures.
Due to increasing resistance, fluoroquinolones are only recommended in cases of
severe penicillin and cephalosporin allergy.
## Inpatient

## Treatment of patients on ward without systemic symptoms of infection
Treat for 4-7 days after source control
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h [M]
Biliary structural abnormality, including stent:
<ADD> Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI] to above regimen
## Treatment of patients in ICU with systemic symptoms of infection
Treat for 4-7 days after source control
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h [R]
Alternative:
Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
Alternative for severe beta-lactam reaction:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

## ER

## Treatment of patients on ward without systemic symptoms of infection
Treat for 4-7 days after source control
Ceftriaxone 2 gm once STAT [M]
Biliary structural abnormality, including stent:
<ADD> Metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT [DI] to above regimen
## Treatment of patients in ICU with systemic symptoms of infection
Treat for 4-7 days after source control
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV once STAT [R]
Alternative:
Cefepime 2 gm IV once STAT [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT [DI]
Alternative for severe beta-lactam reaction:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV once STAT [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT
[DI]
